street.source: Baba data_financials consensus; no margin level target exists; uplift shown is the $85M 2026 savings as % of FY2026 consensus EBITDA, which is already inside 2026 guidance and offset by about $150M of inflation

evidence_of_progress.note: Adjusted EBITDA margin: Q1 2026 10.8% ($232M on $2,156M) vs Q1 2025 $387M on $2,120M (VA actuals), -749 bps; Q2 2026 11.3% vs Q2 2025 $336M ($247M + $89M decline, Lischer) on $2,204M, -395 bps. Sequential +50 bps Q1 to Q2. FY2026 EBITDA guide now at the low end of $1.05B-$1.25B; full-year input inflation raised to about $150M from $60M-$65M; cash flow guide cut to $600M-$700M; net leverage 4.7x. Margin is heavily driven by input costs (secondary fiber, resins, chemicals, energy) and third-party board price indices; not formally disqualified because converting contracts carry cost pass-through, but this is close to the commodity disqualifier. No covenant stress found in the passages read.

verdict: Full external leadership reset into a deeply de-rated stock, but the only numbers are a 2026 cost-savings figure swamped by inflation, forward EBITDA is down 27% in a year, and margins hinge on board prices and input costs, so this is a broken story still being reset rather than an unproven margin gap.
open_questions: Who becomes permanent CFO, and will Rietbroek set a margin or EBITDA target (the market study he mentioned) with Q4 2026 results?
How much of the 2027 consensus margin rebound to 13.9% rests on announced $40-$60 per ton board price increases sticking versus self-help?
Does 4.7x net leverage constrain the plan if 2026 EBITDA lands at or below the $1.05B low end?
